prompt: A money app turns dollars into euros with $e(d) = 0.8d$, then euros into yen with $y(e) = 150e$. Your friend ended up with $12000$ yen. How many dollars did you start with?
hint: You are running the chain BACKWARDS, so undo the LAST machine first. Socks then shoes means shoes come off first.

hints.text: You are running the chain BACKWARDS, so undo the LAST machine first. Socks then shoes means shoes come off first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: a machine doubles, then adds 3, giving 11. Undo backwards: $11 - 3 = 8$, then $8 \div 2 = 4$. Same idea — undo the last step first.
Undo the yen machine by dividing: $12000 \div 150 = 80$ euros. Then undo the euro machine by dividing $80$ by $0.8$.
Dividing gives $80 \div 0.8 = 100$, so you started with $100$ dollars.

explanation: Going forward, the order is dollars to euros and then euros to yen.
Going backward, each machine is undone in reverse order, so first turn yen back into euros: $12000 \div 150 = 80$ euros.
Then turn euros back into dollars: $80 \div 0.8 = 100$, so the starting amount was $100$ dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess and check forward
steps: Then $150 \times 80 = 12000$ yen — exactly the amount your friend has.
